cards.title: Should AI Handle Parenting Tasks?
cards.body: Tech companies now offer eye-movement trackers, personalized podcasts, and optimized nap predictions for parents. The article questions whether parents actually need these AI tools.

cards.title: Rethinking the '18 Summers' Trend
cards.body: This parenting trend pressures parents to optimize summer breaks into memory-making exercises. Critics argue unstructured time is actually what children need.

cards.title: New ADHD Medication Approved by FDA
cards.body: The FDA approved a new non-stimulant ADHD drug in July with stimulant-like effects. A detailed review of clinical trial data shows what parents should know.

cards.title: Understanding Gifted Children's Intensity
cards.body: Gifted children and teenagers often display intense behaviors that confuse parents. Understanding their developmental patterns is key to supporting them effectively.

cards.title: Parental Chaos and Child Psychopathy Risk
cards.body: Recent research links unpredictable parenting to specific traits associated with psychopathy in children. Male children show particular vulnerability to chaotic home environments.

cards.title: Managing Advocacy Burnout for Parents
cards.body: Parents of neurodivergent children often experience burnout from constant advocacy and schooling battles. This article offers mindfulness strategies and self-care tips as school approaches.

cards.title: The Five-Step-No-Tiger Anxiety Method
cards.body: This new technique helps reduce childhood anxiety by transforming vicious worry cycles into positive ones. The method offers practical steps parents can teach their children.

cards.title: Stop Bankrolling Your Adult Child
cards.body: Bailing out adult children financially often sends unintended messages that enable continued dependence. Each bailout reinforces patterns that prevent genuine independence and growth.

cards.title: Asynchronous Development in Gifted Children
cards.body: Bright children often develop unevenly across cognitive and emotional areas, creating unique parenting challenges. Understanding their neuroscience helps parents provide better support.

cards.title: Leading Gen Z: Peter Pan Staff Members
cards.body: Young adults today can perform impressive tasks but resist full adult responsibility, like Peter Pan. Managers and parents must adjust expectations for this generation.

cards.title: The Luteal Phase and Women's Health
cards.body: More women are discussing how the luteal phase affects their mood and energy levels. Understanding this cycle helps women and parents anticipate behavioral and physical changes.
